b: Klad is a drawing app with a fully exposed cli written in rust, that Claude code can use. It can lay down brush strokes one at a time, and each and every stroke remains editable by you or the agent.
Claude Code runs klad commands, the drawing is plain files, and you can open the same file in the Klad editor, which doubles as a fully featured drawing app with layers/brush engine/...
Klad van handle vector art, line art, pixel art, animations,... It's built with game assets in mind, but can do any art style you can teach claude to create really.
There is no image model inside klad. The whole goal is to provide tooling for claude code to use.

The second and third image attached are a couple of examples. The building one shows how easy and consistent it now becomes to ask an agent to make an edit to an existing drawing. This is totally different from the re-rolls you have to do with generative image models. Much less frustrating and with way better results!
This method of working is imo the way forward for human-agent collaboration in art.

How Claude code was used: I've had the idea for a painting app that could work with git for a while now. It would require a special format that is diffsble, and a really performant engine to render all brush strokes in real time as pixels. I didn't want it to be just vectors, as that would not enable paint blending and smudging etc. It would limit the possible art styles.

I had Claude implement this format in Rust, and build a performant render engine around it. Then it was iterating a lot, testing a lot, planning features, testing again... I did a number of performance rounds with Claude code before we got to the point where we are now: detailed 8k drawings with tens of thousands of brush strokes should be no problem for most modern laptops!

Try it yourself at https://github.com/klad-app/klad
Or read the docs at klad.studio
